study.uncertainty: School level, one subject, ChatGPT 3.5 with a guide; read via OECD ch.1 and the Stanford SCALE summary page, not the full report.

sources.citation: Plak, S., Cornelisz, I., Meeter, M. & van Klaveren, C. (2022). Early warning systems for more effective student counselling in higher education: Evidence from a Dutch field experiment. Higher Education Quarterly, 76(1).

study.design: Randomised field experiment
study.sample: First-year students at a large Dutch university (n in full text)
study.context: Netherlands; counsellors received student-level risk information
study.result: EWS predicted at-risk students accurately, but EWS-assisted counselling did not reduce dropout or improve performance.
study.uncertainty: One institution; abstract only; null result may depend on what counsellors did with the flags.

sources.citation: Larrabee Sønderlund, A., Hughes, E. & Smith, J. (2019). The efficacy of learning analytics interventions in higher education: A systematic review. British Journal of Educational Technology, 50(5).

study.design: Systematic review with quality assessment
study.result: Only 11 studies tested interventions; promising but moderate quality; institutions implement with little evidence.
study.uncertainty: Pre-generative-AI literature; review is dated.

sources.citation: Ifenthaler, D. & Yau, J.Y.-K. (2020). Utilising learning analytics to support study success in higher education: a systematic review. Educational Technology Research and Development, 68.

study.design: Systematic review
study.result: Many promising approaches, but rigorous large-scale evidence of effectiveness is still lacking.
study.uncertainty: Pre-generative-AI literature.

sources.citation: Baker, R.S. & Hawn, A. (2022). Algorithmic Bias in Education. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education, 32.

study.design: Narrative review
study.sample: Empirical studies on algorithmic bias in education
study.outcome: Bias by race, gender, nationality, SES, disability (equity)
study.result: Documents concrete bias across groups and pipeline stages; many groups understudied.
study.uncertainty: Not systematic; mixed levels.

sources.citation: Idowu, J.A. (2024). Debiasing Education Algorithms. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education, 34.

study.design: Systematic literature review
study.sample: Studies on fairness of ML in education (dropout, performance prediction, etc.)
study.result: Most studies found no strict fairness-accuracy trade-off; recommends checking data fairness first and assessing impact on end users.
study.uncertainty: Abstract only.

sources.citation: Gándara, D., Anahideh, H., Ison, M.P. & Picchiarini, L. (2024). Inside the Black Box: Detecting and Mitigating Algorithmic Bias Across Racialized Groups in College Student-Success Prediction. AERA Open, 10.

study.design: Secondary analysis; multiple ML models with bias audits
study.sample: Nationally representative US data (Education Longitudinal Study of 2002)
study.result: Models are less accurate for racially minoritised students; common mitigation techniques generally fail to remove the gaps.
study.uncertainty: US data; findings on prediction, not on interventions.

sources.citation: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act), Annex III, point 3 (education and vocational training).

study.design: Legislation
study.result: Annex III point 3(b) lists as high-risk AI systems intended to evaluate learning outcomes, including when those outcomes are used to steer the learning process; 3(a) admission/assignment, 3(c) level of education, 3(d) proctoring.
study.uncertainty: Read via the artificialintelligenceact.eu annex page (EUR-Lex not reachable from our tools). Application dates for Annex III obligations are subject to amendment proposals; check the current Official Journal text. Not legal advice.

sources.citation: Kestin, G., Miller, K., Klales, A., Milbourne, T. & Ponti, G. (2025). AI tutoring outperforms in-class active learning: an RCT introducing a novel research-based design in an authentic educational setting. Scientific Reports, 15.

study.design: Randomised crossover controlled trial
study.sample: N = 194 analysed (course of 233), Harvard introductory physics for life sciences
study.context: US elite university, Fall 2023; two lessons (surface tension, fluid flow)
study.comparison: In-class active learning taught by experienced instructors
study.outcome: Immediate post-test learning gains; time on task; engagement and motivation (satisfaction)
study.result: Median learning gains more than double with the custom AI tutor; effect size ~0.63 (regression) to 0.73-1.3 (other analyses); median 49 min vs 60 min in class; higher engagement and motivation.
study.uncertainty: Immediate post-test only (no retention/transfer); one course, one institution, two topics; tutor built with expert-written, question-specific prompts and pre-written solutions; authors are the course instructors.
study.system: Custom GPT-4-based tutor (PS2 Pal) with structured, instructor-authored prompts

sources.citation: Wu, R. & Yu, Z. (2024). Do AI chatbots improve students learning outcomes? Evidence from a meta-analysis. British Journal of Educational Technology, 55(1), 10-33.

study.design: Meta-analysis
study.result: Large overall effect; larger in higher education; short interventions stronger than long ones (possible novelty effect).
study.uncertainty: Mostly pre-ChatGPT chatbots; heterogeneous outcomes; small studies; many in language learning.

sources.citation: Liu, R., Zenke, C., Liu, C., Holmes, A., Thornton, P. & Malan, D.J. (2024). Teaching CS50 with AI: Leveraging Generative Artificial Intelligence in Computer Science Education. SIGCSE 2024.

study.design: Descriptive deployment report
study.sample: ~70 summer students, thousands online, several hundred on campus
study.outcome: Student perceptions (satisfaction); answer accuracy on forum
study.result: Course-specific tools, designed to guide rather than give answers, were received positively.
study.uncertainty: No comparison group; built and evaluated by course staff.

sources.citation: Guajardo, G., Lanestedt, J. & Friedrich, P.E.L. (2026). Large Language Models in Analytical Processes: Insights from NOKUT's Thematic Analyses of the Third Periodic Review Cycle. NOKUT Report 5/2026.

study.design: Agency practice report; reflective comparison of manual vs LLM-assisted thematic analysis
study.result: Both approaches found many of the same challenges; NotebookLM good at structuring and spotting patterns; confused institution names/abbreviations, needed restructured data and careful prompts; humans must make final judgments.
study.uncertainty: No quantitative agreement measure; public documents only.
study.system: Google NotebookLM (Gemini-based); ChatGPT-4o for prompt refinement

sources.citation: Stasiuk, M., Kukharskyy, V. & Pavlyshenko, B. (2026). Using Large Language Models for Text Analysis in the Evaluation of University Educational Programs. Electronics and Information Technologies, 33.

study.design: Correlational comparison of LLM scores with expert classification
study.outcome: Alignment of LLM scores with expert judgement
